_exempt_platforms_note: exempt_platforms lists (os, arch) a component is ALLOWED to miss (dig_ecosystem#2343). An exemption is legitimate ONLY while the platform is UNRESOLVABLE in AT LEAST ONE signed channel (stable or nightly); it is over-broad/droppable only when the platform is feed-resolvable in EVERY signed channel. As of 2026-08-10 (dig_ecosystem#2555): dig-updater's linux/arm64 resolves in BOTH channels, so its exemption was DROPPED; dig-node's linux/arm64 resolves in stable but NOT nightly, so its exemption is RETAINED (load-bearing for nightly — dropping it would red the #2343 gate on nightly); digstore/dig-dns/dig-app publish no feed-resolvable linux/arm64 default asset in either channel, so theirs are RETAINED. As of 2026-08-24 (dig_ecosystem#2339): dig-chat publishes windows/x64 and linux/x64 ONLY — macOS is blocked on a Developer ID certificate (an unsigned build fails Gatekeeper, so shipping one would deliver an app that cannot open) and linux/arm64 has no build runner, so all three of its exemptions are load-bearing in BOTH channels. dig-chat also cuts no rolling `nightly` release at all, so the nightly leg cannot resolve it; that leg is already expected-red during the #592 fan-out window and an exemption cannot express a missing RELEASE, only a missing platform. The `feedsign --audit-exemptions` drift check (feed.yml PR gate + a daily schedule) REDs only when a declared exemption is resolvable in EVERY channel, and reports a single-channel over-broad as an informational RETAINED note; drop each exemption as its repo publishes that platform in ALL channels. JSON has no comments, hence this sidecar note.
